text:
incident-bot: ALERT: GPU serving pool 'north-america-prod' at 98% GPU utilization; request queue length rising (avg 360s wait). HPA custom metrics show 6m scrape lag. Paging on-call: @Jamie :rotating_light:
Jamie: I'm on it. tagging Priya for metrics, Darren for infra. Morgan pls stand by for customer comms.
Priya: seeing huge backlog from prometheus-adapter -> metrics-server. Adapter logs show 429s / backlog at 1.2M points.
Darren: confirmed pool nearly exhausted. Autoscaler maxReplicas=12 hit; pods are saturated. No recent deploys.
Jamie: quick customer check — any 5xxs from hosted API?
Morgan: yes, telemetry shows elevated 503s on generation endpoints for 3 customers (acct-17, acct-90, acct-220). Latency spikes to ~12s. I've DM'd CS to open incident briefs.
Priya: digging into metrics pipeline. prometheus -> adapter queue depth trace:
```
2026-03-15T02:05:21Z adapter: enqueue 4000 samples
2026-03-15T02:05:30Z adapter: POST /metrics -> 429 backlog
2026-03-15T02:06:10Z kube-metrics-server: scrape timeout
```
Looks like adapter is OOMing GC and falling behind, causing HPA to see stale/custom metrics.
sre-bot: Suggested mitigation: set HPA to fallback on CPU target until custom metrics recover.
Jamie: agree. We'll temporarily relax HPA to allow more replicas and also restart metrics-adapter. Plan: 1) increase HPA maxReplicas to 20 2) restart prometheus-adapter deployment (rolling) 3) add admission annotation to force immediate scale if queue > 0.
Darren: applying step 1 now.
Darren: `kubectl patch hpa inference-workers -n prod -p '{"spec": {"maxReplicas": 20}}'`
Jamie: done. monitoring for scale events...
Priya: preparing adapter restart. I'm going to scale it down then up to clear local queue, then tail logs.
Priya: `kubectl -n monitoring rollout restart deployment prometheus-adapter`
Priya: tailing logs: `kubectl -n monitoring logs -l app=prometheus-adapter -f --tail=50`
MetricsBot: metrics pipeline alert cleared? Adapter restart returned pods healthy after ~45s, but I still see 60s scrape lag in custom metrics.
Jamie: HPA reacted, new replicas started; GPU pool scale lagging because cloud autoscaler queue is saturated. We need to bump reserved capacity or trigger manual pool scale.
Darren: requesting manual add of 6 GPUs to pool. K8s autoscaler is limited by quota currently. Requesting approval from infra lead (cc: @Darren).
Darren: I've opened cloud request ticket CLD-8342 to add instances in na region. ETA ~3m for allocation.
Morgan: customer comms: posting status on status.redwood.ai -> brief noting degraded performance for some customers, engineers investigating; ETA initial mitigation 15m.
Jamie: one more mitigation: route non-critical traffic to cheaper CPU-backed fallback model to reduce GPU pressure. Can we flip routing rule?
Priya: yes, runbook step: update router config in config-store 'routing/v1' to route model:generator-large -> generator-large-cpu for accounts in beta group. Command:
```
kubectl -n config apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: routing-v1
data:
  override: |
    routes:
      - match: "/v1/generate"
        predicates:
          - header: "x-account-tier"
            values: ["beta"]
        destination: "generator-large-cpu"
EOF
```
Priya: applied routing override for beta accounts. This should reduce GPU pressure by ~8-12%.
MetricsBot: custom metrics lag improving: 30s -> 10s. HPA now seeing fresh metrics.
Jamie: cloud pool scaled +6 GPUs (CLD-8342 completed). New GPU nodes ready. Pod scheduling resumed faster. Queue length dropping.
Morgan: CS updated customers; two customers saw degraded experience but no data loss. Morgan: CS will follow up with targeted postmortem and credits if SLAs breached.
Darren: good to confirm autoscaler config afterwards — we hit quota/reserved capacity limits that prevented smooth autoscale. Need followup: increase soft limits and add circuit to spill to cpu fallback earlier.
Jamie: on-call handoff note: I'm keeping the channel open for 30m monitoring, then handoff to @Morgan for post-incident followups. If anything spikes, page me.
Priya: followups: investigate adapter OOM cause (heap growth under burst), add request batching and backpressure, add metrics to detect adapter backlog and alert earlier.
Darren: infra followups: increase cloud quota for gpu-pool, add proactive pre-warm policy based on forecasted traffic, and document manual override steps for urgent scaling.
Morgan: I'll draft incident body and notify legal/finance for potential SLA implications.
Jamie: status update: mitigation successful, queue stabilized, HPA now stable on fresh metrics, customer impact limited. Closing active mitigation in 12m unless otherwise noted. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident was acknowledged at 4444444444 and marked live-mitigation. Current severity: SEV2 (degraded service).
Jamie: handing off to Morgan at 4444444555. Thanks team.
Morgan: taking over for postmortem. will compile timeline + notes.
